tagline: Global leader in mining and cement technologies delivering sustainable productivity solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: Revenue of DKK 20.2 billion in 2024 reflecting FLSmidth's overall performance in the mining and cement industries, despite uncertain macroeconomic conditions and significant strategic transitions.
company_description: FLSmidth & Co. A/S provides flowsheet technology and service solutions for the mining industries in Denmark, the United States of America, Canada, Chile, Brazil, Peru, Australia, North and South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia. The company operates through three segments: Service; Products; and Pumps, Cyclones & Valves (PC&V). The company offers mineral processing equipment, such as hydrocyclones and REFLUX classifiers; cone and roll crushers, crushing stations, gyratory and jaw crushers, and sizers; centrifuges, thickeners and clarifiers, and filters; apron and belt feeders, buffalo and vibrating feeders, mine hoists, hybrid apron feeders, and mine shaft equipment; and attrition scrubbers, column and forced-air flotation cells, mixed and self-aspirated flotation cells, and REFLUX and coarse flotation cells. It also includes ball and vertical fine grinding mills, and SAG and AG mills; laboratory equipment, such as automated laboratories, crushing, dividing, drying, pulverizing, and thermogravimetric analysis equipment; carbon ADR plants and regeneration kilns, precious metals electrowinning and refinery, gravity concentration, mercury retort and abatement

risks.title: Dependence on a complex and high-risk global supply chain
risks.summary: FLSmidth relies on more than 9,000 supplier groups globally, with 32% of expenditures concentrated in countries at high risk of forced labor. A supplier failure or supply disruption in these regions (India, China, South Africa, Chile) could disrupt the delivery of critical technology solutions to mining and cement customers.
risks.score_rationale: Risk repeatedly and centrally mentioned in the document (dominant supply chain section); strong language ('vast and diverse', 'high-risk countries', '32% of total supplier spend in high forced-labour-risk countries'); increasing trend linked to geographic concentration in mining; critical category for a global industrial equipment provider.

risks.title: Risk of forced labor and modern slavery in the value chain
risks.summary: FLSmidth operates in countries classified as high-risk according to the Global Slavery Index, with suppliers and partners exposed to forced labor, human trafficking, and child labor practices. A public association with such practices—even indirectly through a subcontractor—could lead to contract losses, regulatory sanctions, and lasting brand reputation damage.
risks.score_rationale: Core subject of the filing (Modern Slavery Statement); explicit language on reputational risk ('reputational risk involved with our customers and suppliers potentially using forced labour'); stable trend but under heightened scrutiny; high weight for a company operating in high-risk mining jurisdictions.

risks.title: Non-compliance with modern slavery regulations (Australia, Canada)
risks.summary: FLSmidth is subject to legal reporting obligations on modern slavery in Australia (via FLSmidth Pty Ltd, ~600 employees, AUD 573M revenue) and Canada (FLSmidth Ltd, ~150 employees, CAD 165M). Failure to meet these reporting requirements or identification of due diligence process failures would expose the company to legal penalties and exclusion from public procurement markets.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly addressed by two national laws (Modern Slavery Act 2018 Australia; Fighting Against Forced Labour and Child Labour in Supply Chains Act Canada); compliance-focused language ('reporting entity', 'approved by board'); upward trend with proliferation of ESG laws; moderate weight as FLSmidth appears to be in active compliance.

risks.title: Geographic concentration of operations in high-risk countries
risks.summary: Urbanization trends and geographic concentration of mining opportunities compel FLSmidth to operate in countries classified as high-risk by the Responsible Business Alliance. Political instability, conflicts, or regulatory changes in these jurisdictions (particularly in Africa, Latin America, Asia) could compromise operational continuity and employee safety.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned ('wide range of countries classified as high-risk based on country classification indices'); direct language on geopolitical exposure linked to mining concentration; upward trend with urbanization and deposit concentration; critical category for a global mining equipment provider.

risks.title: Conflict minerals risk in the supply chain
risks.summary: As a provider of solutions to the mining industry, FLSmidth is exposed to the risk of sourcing conflict minerals (tantalum, tin, tungsten, gold: 3TG: and cobalt). Inadvertent use of these minerals from conflict zones could lead to regulatory violations (Dodd-Frank, EU conflict minerals regulation) and significant reputational damage.
risks.score_rationale: Industry-specific risk addressed via a dedicated sub-policy (Conflict Minerals Sub-policy) and focus on 3TG and cobalt; language indicating active monitoring ('updated our conflict minerals policy in 2024'); stable trend with recent update; moderate but sector-specific weight.

risks.title: Insufficient internal training on human rights and compliance
risks.summary: Despite a mandatory human rights training requirement for all new employees, only 74% of white-collar employees completed the e-learning module in 2024, leaving a quarter of staff potentially unaware of modern slavery and human rights violation risks. This gap increases the risk of undetected incidents in operations and the supply chain.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly identified internal operational risk: e-learning training completion rate at only 74% (target not met, up from 60% in 2023); moderate language ('we acknowledge that more progress is needed'); improving but insufficient trend; limited but revealing organizational vulnerability.

risks.title: Organizational fragmentation in procurement management across Business Lines
risks.summary: FLSmidth's supply chain is managed in a fragmented manner across Business Lines (Service, Product, PCV, Cement), with regional and central procurement teams having distinct mandates. This fragmentation creates risks of inconsistent application of ethical standards, cost duplication, and increased vulnerability to local supply disruptions.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly described structural risk ('divided across different Business Lines with rather independent setups'); nuanced language acknowledging fragmentation while highlighting alignment efforts; stable trend with partial centralization efforts; significant weight for ESG standard consistency and operational resilience.

risks.title: Reputational risk related to ESG practices of mining and cement clients
risks.summary: FLSmidth faces indirect reputational risk from human rights violations by its mining and cement clients, particularly in low-governance jurisdictions. Such association, even without direct liability, could harm FLSmidth's reputation among ESG investors, regulators, and institutional clients.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned risk ('reputational risk involved with our customers potentially using forced labour'); FLSmidth has implemented human rights clauses in customer contracts and client due diligence; upward trend with growing ESG regulatory pressure; moderate but strategic weight for a leading B2B supplier.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the provided documents. FLSmidth does not position AI as a strategic lever in its current operations.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or advanced automation tools in the Modern Slavery Act Statement 2024.
Strategic priorities mentioned focus on organizational transformation, decarbonization (MissionZero), and operational simplification.
No mention of products or services incorporating AI in the Mining or Cement segments.
